requirement: The system must maintain a unique internal Supplier ID for each approved supplier organization.
evidence: supplier.supplier_code SUP-nnnnnn, unique; created from the supplier profile or the seed.

requirement: The system must maintain supplier legal/display name, status and approved organization metadata.
evidence: Legal name, country, status and contact details kept (profile page). No supplier approval metadata or onboarding.

requirement: The system must support multiple supplier users with role-based access to their own organization data.
evidence: Release 0.5 has one shared supplier account (admin). Multi-user, role-based supplier access is deferred to the RBAC phase.

requirement: Supplier users must not access another supplier's records unless an explicitly approved cross-supplier relationship exists.
evidence: Every supplier-portal query is scoped to the account supplier; another supplier record answers 404 (tests: supplier isolation).

requirement: The system must support supplier activation, suspension and deactivation without deleting historical records.
evidence: supplier.status column exists and history is never deleted; no screen to suspend or deactivate.

requirement: The system must associate external EDI partner identities with the relevant supplier organization.
evidence: EDI partner identities are part of the X12 phase.

requirement: The system should support multiple trading-partner profiles or endpoints for one supplier where required.
evidence: EDI trading-partner profiles are part of the X12 phase.

requirement: The system must record who created or changed supplier and partner configuration.
evidence: Profile create/change audited (CREATE/UPDATE_SUPPLIER_PROFILE); no EDI partner configuration yet.

requirement: The system must create a stable, unique, company-generated Product ID.
evidence: product.product_code PRD-nnnnnnn generated by the database.

requirement: A Product ID must remain stable across multiple manufacturing/traceability records.
evidence: Products are matched by supplier + company part number and reused by every shipment.

requirement: The system must store product name, description, category and governed core metadata.
evidence: Name, description, category and governed JSONB attributes per product version.

requirement: The system must support multiple supplier/manufacturer part-number mappings per product.
evidence: product_identifier supports many identifiers; the form and CSV capture the company part number and one supplier part number.

requirement: Each alternate identifier must retain identifier type, issuing organization and relevant scope.
evidence: Identifier type and normalized value stored; issuing organization is implied by the supplier; no explicit scope field.

requirement: The system must prevent uncontrolled duplicate product creation through configured matching and review rules.
evidence: Duplicate products prevented by the supplier + company part number match; no fuzzy matching or review rules.

requirement: The system must preserve product version history and the current approved version.
evidence: product_version history with current_approved_version_id; approved versions immutable (trigger).

requirement: Product category definitions and applicable attribute sets must be configurable and versioned.
evidence: Categories and attribute definitions are versioned in the database; changed through migrations, no admin screen.

requirement: The system must distinguish supplier-provided product identifiers from internal identifiers.
evidence: Identifier types COMPANY_PART_NUMBER and SUPPLIER_PART_NUMBER are kept apart.

requirement: The system must assign a unique Traceability ID to each traceability record.
evidence: traceability_record.traceability_code TRC-nnnnnnn.

requirement: Each traceability record must reference exactly one Product ID in the initial model.
evidence: Each record references exactly one product (NOT NULL foreign key).

requirement: The system must support manufacturing attributes such as heat, batch, material grade and manufacturing date where applicable.
evidence: Heat, batch, material and manufacturing date supported (attributes and heat/batch tables).

requirement: The system must support optional serial-number collections linked to a traceability record.
evidence: Serial-number collections (traceability_version_serial); CSV column serial_numbers.

requirement: The data model must not assume a one-to-one heat-to-batch relationship where the manufacturing process permits multiple associations.
evidence: Heat and batch are many-to-many (batch_heat); a version can list several heats.

requirement: The system must retain the issuer and uniqueness scope of external heat, batch and serial identifiers.
evidence: Heats and batches are scoped per supplier (issuer); no separate uniqueness-scope field.

requirement: The system must support traceability-record versioning and approved history.
evidence: traceability_version history; release 0.5 supersedes the previous version on every changed save.

requirement: The system must preserve source and provenance for submitted and corrected values.
evidence: Version source (PORTAL/SEED), creator and time recorded; no field-level provenance of corrections.

requirement: Administrators must be able to define attributes without requiring a code deployment for every new optional field.
evidence: A new CSV column registers a new attribute definition automatically; no code change.

requirement: An attribute definition must specify type, scope, applicability, cardinality and validation metadata.
evidence: attribute_definition holds type, scope, category, required, allowed values, unit, comparison rule, label_checked.

requirement: The system must support category-specific requiredness and conditional validation.
evidence: Requiredness per category; no conditional validation rules.

requirement: The system must version attribute definitions and preserve historical interpretation.
evidence: Definitions are versioned (e.g. heat_number v2); deprecated versions are kept for history.

requirement: The system must support governed code lists and units of measure.
evidence: Allowed values and units stored; no unit-of-measure conversion or managed code-list screens.

requirement: The system should support configurable cross-field validation rules.
evidence: Cross-field validation rules are not implemented.

requirement: Attribute visibility must be controlled by object scope and access policy.
evidence: Attributes are separated by scope (product / traceability); no per-role visibility.

requirement: The system must support upload of approved technical evidence types including MTC, CoC and inspection reports.
evidence: Document types MTC, COC, RT_REPORT, INSPECTION_REPORT, DRAWING, OTHER.

requirement: Each document must be associated with the correct product/traceability context and submission version.
evidence: Each document is attached to the shipment record and the version it was uploaded to.

requirement: The system must store metadata including document type, file name, media type, size, revision and source.
evidence: Type, file name, media type, size, revision and storage key stored.

requirement: The system must preserve document history when a supplier replaces or revises a file.
evidence: New uploads never overwrite; earlier documents stay listed with their version.

requirement: Documents must be private and downloadable only after authorization.
evidence: Private bucket, 5-minute signed links. By stakeholder decision (v0.5) a scanned QR label also opens its own record certificates without sign-in. Decided 27 Nov 2026: sign-in required again (Phase 1).

requirement: The system should compute and retain a content hash for integrity verification.
evidence: SHA-256 of every file stored (document.sha256).

requirement: The system should validate file size, extension, media type and malware-scan result before publication.
evidence: Size (15 MB), extension, declared and sniffed media type checked; no malware scanning.

requirement: A supplier must be able to save a draft without publishing it.
evidence: Removed in v0.5 by decision (saves are live at once). Built in v0.1-v0.4; kept on branch archive/roles-and-review. A PO match check is proposed in its place (SPIR-SCP-001).

requirement: A supplier must explicitly submit a draft for company review.
evidence: Removed in v0.5 by decision. Built in v0.1-v0.4 (archive branch).

requirement: The system must route submitted versions to an authorized reviewer or review queue.
evidence: Removed in v0.5 by decision. Review queue built in v0.1-v0.4 (archive branch).

requirement: A reviewer must be able to approve or reject a submitted version.
evidence: Removed in v0.5 by decision. Approve/reject built in v0.1-v0.4 (archive branch).

requirement: A rejection must include a reason or actionable correction feedback.
evidence: Removed in v0.5 by decision. Mandatory rejection reason built in v0.1-v0.4 (archive branch).

requirement: A rejected version must be correctable and resubmittable with history preserved.
evidence: Removed in v0.5 by decision. Correct-and-resubmit built in v0.1-v0.4 (archive branch).

requirement: A new pending version must not overwrite the currently approved version.
evidence: A change never edits a version: it adds a new one and the previous one is kept as SUPERSEDED. Without review, the new version is live at once.

requirement: Only approved versions may be returned by the company QR retrieval flow.
evidence: QR scans return only the APPROVED (live) version and no history (test: public scan).

requirement: Approval must record reviewer, timestamp, decision, comments and version.
evidence: No approval step in v0.5. Reviewer, time, decision and comment were recorded in v0.1-v0.4.

requirement: The system should support configurable multi-level approval in a future release.
evidence: Multi-level approval is a future release item.

requirement: The system must create one QR token per traceability record under the selected QR model.
evidence: One ACTIVE token per record (unique index); issued on the first save.

requirement: The QR must contain an opaque platform locator, not embedded sensitive manufacturing data.
evidence: The QR holds only a random 16-character token in a link; no product data.

requirement: The QR must not grant access without successful user authentication and authorization.
evidence: By stakeholder decision (v0.5) scans are open to anyone. Rate limited; shows one record. Enforced sign-in in v0.1-v0.4. Decided 27 Nov 2026: sign-in for every scan again (Phase 1).

requirement: The resolution service must return the latest approved version for the traceability record.
evidence: Resolution returns the current approved version.

requirement: The system must support QR activation, revocation and replacement without changing the Traceability ID.
evidence: Revoke and replace (rotate) keep the Traceability ID (tests).

requirement: The system should provide controlled print/download output for QR labels.
evidence: A4 sticker sheets (8/14/21), 300 dpi PNG, CSV links; every code decoded again before printing.

requirement: The system must prevent revoked, unknown or inactive tokens from resolving to business data.
evidence: Unknown token 404, revoked 410; no business data returned.

requirement: QR access events should be logged according to access-audit policy.
evidence: QR_RESOLVE, QR_RESOLVE_UNKNOWN, QR_RESOLVE_REVOKED and DOWNLOAD_DOCUMENT_VIA_QR audited.

evidence: X12 EDI intake is outside this proof of concept (planned phase). The canonical model has source EDI ready.

requirement: The initial supplier information profile should evaluate X12 832 for catalog/product data and X12 841 for technical information.
evidence: X12 EDI intake is outside this proof of concept (planned phase). The canonical model has source EDI ready.

requirement: The system must validate interchange, functional-group and transaction-set control structures.
evidence: X12 EDI intake is outside this proof of concept (planned phase). The canonical model has source EDI ready.

evidence: X12 EDI intake is outside this proof of concept (planned phase). The canonical model has source EDI ready.

requirement: The system must translate accepted messages into the canonical internal model.
evidence: X12 EDI intake is outside this proof of concept (planned phase). The canonical model has source EDI ready.

requirement: The system must keep raw inbound payloads or a governed immutable archive reference for audit and replay.
evidence: X12 EDI intake is outside this proof of concept (planned phase). The canonical model has source EDI ready.

requirement: The system must detect duplicate/replayed messages using partner and control-number/idempotency rules.
evidence: X12 EDI intake is outside this proof of concept (planned phase). The canonical model has source EDI ready.

requirement: The system must track processing status at interchange, group, transaction and business-submission levels.
evidence: X12 EDI intake is outside this proof of concept (planned phase). The canonical model has source EDI ready.

requirement: The system should generate 997 or 999 acknowledgments according to the partner agreement and selected profile.
evidence: X12 EDI intake is outside this proof of concept (planned phase). The canonical model has source EDI ready.

requirement: The system should use 824 for application/business content feedback where agreed and supported by the partner profile.
evidence: X12 EDI intake is outside this proof of concept (planned phase). The canonical model has source EDI ready.

requirement: The system must distinguish technical acceptance from business approval/publication.
evidence: Planned with EDI. Design keeps technical acceptance separate from publication.

requirement: EDI messages must not directly publish product or traceability data without the configured company approval process.
evidence: Planned with EDI. Requires the approval workflow to return first.

requirement: The system must maintain a versioned X12 implementation guide and mapping configuration for each supported partner/profile.
evidence: X12 EDI intake is outside this proof of concept (planned phase). The canonical model has source EDI ready.

requirement: The system must quarantine malformed, unsupported or suspicious messages without losing operational evidence.
evidence: X12 EDI intake is outside this proof of concept (planned phase). The canonical model has source EDI ready.

requirement: Administrators must be able to manage product categories, attribute definitions and controlled lists under permission control.
evidence: Categories, attributes and label profiles maintained through migrations and the seed CSV; no admin screens.

requirement: Administrators must be able to activate/suspend suppliers and EDI partner profiles.
evidence: No screen to activate or suspend suppliers; no EDI partners.

requirement: The system must maintain audit records for security-sensitive and business-significant actions.
evidence: audit_event is append-only (trigger) and covers sign-in, imports, QR, documents, label checks.

requirement: The system should provide operational views for pending approvals and failed EDI processing.
evidence: Label check history available; no pending-approval view (no approvals in v0.5), no EDI.

requirement: Operational reprocessing must be permission-controlled and auditable.
evidence: No reprocessing operations yet.

requirement: The company inspection experience must support camera-based still-image capture from approved mobile/tablet cameras and other certified camera devices.
evidence: Camera still capture (getUserMedia) and photo upload in the company portal.

requirement: The platform must support approved external QR/1D/2D barcode readers through one or more adapters (for example HID/keyboard-wedge, USB, Bluetooth, serial, network or vendor SDK where applicable).
evidence: Camera/webcam decoding (ZXing) and HID keyboard-wedge scanners; no serial, SDK or network scanner adapters.

requirement: The platform must abstract device-specific drivers, SDKs, connection handling and events from the core business and validation logic.
evidence: Device adapters in web/src/devices (camera, barcode, OCR, scanner) separate from business logic.

requirement: The platform must maintain a configurable compatibility profile for device model, firmware/driver, host OS, connection mode, supported symbologies/resolutions and tested application version.
evidence: No device compatibility profile.

requirement: The capture flow must request and use camera/device permissions explicitly and provide clear device selection, ready, disconnected and error states.
evidence: Explicit camera permission, device selection, ready / error states.

requirement: The system must associate each capture with an authenticated user, device/profile where available, timestamp, session/correlation ID and target validation run.
evidence: Label checks record user, time and correlation ID; no device/profile identity.

requirement: The system must handle device disconnection, unavailable permissions, unsupported formats, poor capture and duplicate scan events without corrupting registry data.
evidence: Permission denial, unsupported formats and poor captures handled; duplicate scan events not formally de-duplicated.

requirement: Where offline capture is enabled, the client must queue encrypted evidence and clearly show that registry validation is pending until synchronization and server-side comparison complete.
evidence: No offline capture.

requirement: Device administration must be separate from business approval authority and must be permission-controlled and audited.
evidence: No device administration.

requirement: The platform should support both direct client-to-device integration and a managed local/edge connector for devices that cannot be accessed directly by the browser or mobile app.
evidence: Direct browser-to-device only; no edge connector.

requirement: The system must accept image evidence from approved camera/capture devices and create a traceable capture record.
evidence: Each label check stores the image as evidence with its SHA-256.

requirement: The OCR pipeline must support configurable image quality checks and preprocessing, including orientation, crop, rotation, perspective correction and image enhancement as required by the selected engine.
evidence: Manual crop, upscale, rotate, greyscale and contrast; image quality warnings. No automatic perspective correction.

requirement: The OCR capability must be provider/engine agnostic through an adapter contract, permitting an approved on-device, edge, on-premises or cloud engine.
evidence: OCR runs behind a browser adapter; the server receives text and words, so the engine can change.

requirement: The extraction layer must support label profiles, field aliases and versioned mappings for different suppliers, manufacturers, product categories and sticker layouts.
evidence: Versioned label profiles (RECEIVING_LABELS v1) with aliases, patterns and fallbacks.

requirement: The system must support extraction of configurable attribute candidates such as part number, manufacturer/supplier identifier, heat number, batch/lot number, material grade, serial number and manufacturing date.
evidence: Part number, PO, line, quantity, heat, pattern, RT, supplier, description, material, revision, country.

requirement: For each candidate field, the system must preserve raw text, normalized candidate, confidence score where supplied, source image region/bounding box where available, extraction method and engine/profile version.
evidence: Raw text, normalized value, confidence and bounding box kept per field.

requirement: The system must support concurrent QR/barcode decoding and OCR from the same capture where applicable.
evidence: ZXing and Tesseract run on the same capture; a barcode wins over a weak OCR read.

requirement: The resolver must match using deterministic, namespaced identifiers and approved combination rules; ambiguous or conflicting matches must require user review.
evidence: resolver-v2 with deterministic identifier combinations; ambiguity goes to the user.

requirement: The validation service must compare extracted candidates against a pinned approved product/traceability version and its applicable attribute definitions and validation rules.
evidence: Comparison against the pinned approved version and its attribute definitions.

requirement: The interface must display a field-level validation matrix including approved value, observed OCR value, normalized value, confidence, comparison status and review/discrepancy note.
evidence: Field-level validation matrix with approved, observed, normalized, confidence and result.

requirement: The system must support per-attribute normalization and comparison rules, including exact, controlled-alias, format-normalized and tolerance-based comparisons only where explicitly configured.
evidence: Per-attribute methods: identifier, code, date, decimal, integer, quantity, name, text.

requirement: The operator must be able to review or correct an OCR candidate without overwriting the raw OCR evidence; manual corrections must be attributed and audited.
evidence: Operator confirm/correct per field; raw OCR kept; attributed and audited (test).

requirement: OCR or validation results must not directly update, approve or publish product/traceability master data. Any correction must follow a separately authorized submission and approval workflow.
evidence: Label checks and discrepancies never change registry data (test).

requirement: The system must support distinct results for match, mismatch, low confidence, unreadable, missing on label, missing in registry, not applicable, not checked and manual review required.
evidence: Nine field results plus REVIEW_REQUIRED; five overall statuses.

requirement: The system should allow an operator to create a discrepancy record containing selected image evidence, field differences, severity, comments and assignment/status.
evidence: Discrepancy records with fields, severity and comment.

requirement: The system must retain the identity/version of the approved record, label profile, attribute definitions, normalization rules and OCR engine used for a validation run.
evidence: Run pins record version, label profile version and rule versions (compare-v2/overall-v2/resolver-v2).

requirement: The system should support configurable confidence thresholds by field and label profile; a threshold must not by itself convert an unequal value into a match.
evidence: Per-profile thresholds; a threshold never turns unequal values into a match.

requirement: The system should provide a review path for labels that do not match a known profile, including manual field association and controlled profile onboarding.
evidence: Unknown layouts can be read and corrected field by field; no profile onboarding flow.
